extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, research-integrity professionals, sleuths, and readers interested in retractions
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and extract practical standards from COPE's updated retraction and Expression of Concern (EOC) guidance for scholarly journals, focusing on when and how to retract or flag problematic papers. Intended to inform editorial policy and corrective-action decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship verification and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Retract articles when 'authorship of the publication cannot be verified or there are serious concerns about accountability for the research.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated guidance explicitly lists unverifiable authorship or serious accountability concerns as grounds for retraction — this addresses situations such as fictitious authorship and author identity issues tied to paper mills or third-party manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any form of misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Retract papers that involve 'any form of misrepresentation,' including 'deception; fraud (eg, a paper mill); identity theft or fictitious authorship; or undisclosed involvement of artificial intelligence (AI).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is broad and covers deceptive practices before, during, or after submission; undeclared AI use and identity theft are specifically enumerated as examples warranting retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compromised or manipulated peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Retract when the peer review process has been compromised, including specific mechanisms: 'fake reviewers, paper mill use, or citation manipulation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New guidance expands the earlier, more general reason ('compromised or manipulated peer review') by listing concrete compromises; these are explicit grounds for retraction rather than merely a flag for further inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Batch retraction transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: When issuing mass/batch retractions, notices should 'clearly state that systematic, coordinated, and widespread manipulation of the publication process has been identified and that the article is one of a group of articles affected by the same process of manipulation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large-scale retractions, notices must make clear the systemic nature of the problem and the article's membership in an affected group so readers understand context and scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer re-review for potentially uninvolved authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should offer the chance for the article to be 're-reviewed' before the retraction notices are published when authors may not have been involved in the mass fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This safeguard aims to protect authors who were swept up in batch retractions despite not participating in misconduct; it implies a procedural step before finalizing retraction for such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of retractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Retraction notices should be published 'as soon as possible after the editor is convinced that the publication is seriously flawed, misleading, or otherwise unreliable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance emphasizes prompt publication of retraction notices and explicitly lists things that should not delay retraction (authors/institutions not cooperating, a not-yet-published letter/comment raising concerns, the outcome of an institutional investigation). COPE did not mandate a fixed deadline, noting process length can vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressions of Concern (EOC) issuance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish an EOC if an investigation or resolution of a credible concern will take 'some time (eg, several months)' or 'if an editor of a journal determines that concerns raised about an article are substantial and credible enough to warrant alerting readers, but insufficient information is available to decide whether a correction or retraction is required.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EOC guidance sets out three possible resolutions following an EOC: no changes needed, a correction or retraction is required, or concerns were unable to be resolved. The EOC can also remain a permanent outcome in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit to third-party reporters/sleuths
rubrics_metrics.description: If concerns about the article were raised by a third party, 'their name could be included in the retraction notice, if relevant, and with permission.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COPE recommends acknowledging third-party contributors when appropriate and with consent; the article notes sleuths often prioritize removal of unreliable papers over receiving credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference external investigations and follow standards; no paywall
rubrics_metrics.description: Retraction notices should reference external investigations when relevant, follow National Information Standards Organization (NISO) best practices, and not be behind a paywall or other access barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures notices are transparent, standardized, and accessible to readers and the scholarly record; points to following external standards (NISO) and avoiding restricted-access notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive content and clarity of retraction notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Retraction notices must provide clear, specific information about why a paper was retracted — mere statements like 'this paper has been retracted' are inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should adhere to content recommendations so readers understand the nature of the problem; include reasons, references to investigations where relevant, and sufficient detail to inform the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow editorial action without waiting for institutional assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should be able to make decisions about editorial action without deferring to or waiting for the results of institutional assessments of researcher behavior or publication integrity in the majority of cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The updated guidance deemphasizes overreliance on institutional investigations and calls for clearer statements so journal staff know they can take editorial actions independently when warranted.
